title: Octave starts a playback the server owns
description: Serves Goal 1: "Playback never surprises a viewer."; "Any film plays, and plays well."; "What can't be done is said plainly."; "Access is enforced everywhere.". Absorbs JS-040 and JS-181.
acceptanceCriteria: An app asks to play a title, with what its device can play and the tracks chosen; the answer says how it will play (as it is, converted, re-encoded) and why.
The media link opens that one playback, carries no account credential, and stops working when the viewer or the operator ends the playback; it survives a long pause.

On Android TV's player (Media3 on an emulator: a minimal player in the server's test tree, or Octave's Android TV app once it exists) and in Octave (or, until JS-190 and JS-150, the native browser check): a title that plays as it is, one whose container is converted, and one re-encoded with a non-default audio track and an image subtitle each start, play 30 seconds and seek, with picture, sound and subtitles right from the first frame.
Progress becomes the viewer's place on every device.
A play that cannot start now, or a conversion that loses something (such as audio channels), carries a reason Octave can explain, with when to retry where retrying helps.
A worker killed mid-film costs no picture, as today.
Every capability it adds is in the published contract (JS-183) and passes its conformance check.
One playback's id is in every log line of it, from the play request to each segment, its job and its worker's ffmpeg; docs/running.md shows how to follow one.

The read each media request makes of its playback and its access is added to the stress run; its 99th percentile at 1,600 viewers is recorded against today's at 1,600 viewers, and one more than 20% above it comes to the product owner as a brief before merge.

A playback lives while its app reports on it; one with no report for 90 seconds has ended, never revives, and its link is refused with that reason and the action to start again. A media request does not keep a playback alive. A play with no position starts at the viewer's place with their picks. On the Media3 player, a playback ended by the server while the app plays is noticed by the app within 10 seconds. If the viewer was watching, a new playback starts at their place with nothing shown, or the refusal of the new play is shown with its reason. The player is never left buffering.
notes: It builds the two players its criterion 3 plays on: a minimal Media3 player on an emulator and a minimal browser player, both in the server's test tree, driving only jellyscale's own API. They become the e2e gate at the cutover (JS-194) until Octave's builds take over (JS-190, JS-150). #222, #224, #295: the one-playback link, the device saying what it cannot play, and a reason when audio loses channels. Note, not a criterion: it writes end and failure messages from the start, so JS-197 adds delivery only. Amended 2026-11-27 by D-20261127-media3-link-end-message, decided by the product owner: criterion 10 gains the Media3 playback-end check.
